reconcile.connective: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown close the two-day gap by splitting the act in two: the release was decreed on the twenty-fifth and only carried into effect on the twenty-seventh.

discrepancy.connective: Keil & Delitzsch concede the two-day gap is a real textual fault, tracing it to a copyist's slip rather than reading the two numbers as compatible.

excerpts.excerpt_text: five and twentieth day--but in Kg2 25:27, it is "the twenty-seventh day." Probably on the twenty-fifth the decree for his elevation was given, and the preparations for it made by releasing him from prison; and on the twenty-seventh day it was carried into effect.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB names the two-day discrepancy explicitly and offers the standard decree-then-execution harmonization for it.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The difference of date, "on the twenty-fifth of the month" (Jer 52:31), and "on the twenty-seventh of the month" in 2 Kings, has arisen through the entrance of a clerical error into one text or the other.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Keil & Delitzsch concede the date conflict is real, attributing it to a scribal/copying error in transmission rather than harmonizing the two numbers as both accurate.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley catalogs this exact pair under "Historical Discrepancies": "His deliverance on the twenty-seventh day of the month, 2 Kings xxv. 27; on the twenty-fifth day, Jer. lii. 31 (a mistake as to a single numeral letter)" (p. 400).
